name: vegetable-rebuild-v4
description: THE TWO CARDS THAT ARE THE SUIT, SWITCHED OFF. Read this before reading the arm, because it is the same caveat the Wheat and Orchard arms carry and it is load-bearing: a suit rebuild is a data-and-handler change, not a set of numbers, so NO OVERLAY CAN EXPRESS "the Vegetable suit as it was". A knob cannot un-write a Farmstead that minted a coin into one that moves a card, cannot restore a Barn that refunded freight instead of refunding a build, cannot un-turn three Tier 3 cards from GROW-gated into printed ACTIONs, and cannot take the hand payment back off a balloon. What it CAN reach is the one thing the whole rebuild was built around: V5 The Coastal Trading Depot and V6 The Trade Depot, the only cards in 105 that touch the island's demand tokens. Base is the rebuild with them in, this cell is the rebuild with them out, and the delta is what mutable demand tokens are worth - which is the question §4 of the ticket exists to answer, because they cost more engine than the rest of the suit put together. If the delta is nothing, the honest move is to say so rather than to ship the rules. Every other pass condition - BALLOON MOVES PER GAME up sharply from 5.1 with a Vegetable seat taking well over an even share (the draft's central prediction), a VEGETABLE SEAT'S VISITS PER TURN at or above 0.52 (its central risk, and in tension with the first BY DESIGN, because flights cost hand cards and an empty hand cannot visit), V13/V14/V15 play rate up sharply from the ~2% Tier 3 baseline and V11 up from 4% and V10 up from 1%, Vegetable's win rate up from 31.5% toward the 37.5% even share WITHOUT PASSING IT, median game length flat with a Vegetable seat present (V7 and V14 both grant deliveries and V5/V6 make tiles payable that were not, so this is the one that could go wrong quietly), and reshuffles per played deck flat - is before-and-after against the committed reference run, not against this cell. Two warnings on the instrument itself. (1) THE BOTS CANNOT JUDGE V5'S DENIAL USE: outcome.ts prices what a seat gains and never rival harm, so every swap they take is self-serving and this arm reads the card as pure upside. Whether swapping a token out from under a rival's hoarded pair lands as clever or as the predecessor's number one BGG dislike is a table question and only a table question. (2) REPORT THE MAGENTA BALLOON'S TAKE RATE: its "Gain £4" is a solitaire coin faucet the coin rule forbids, and V8 The Regional Depot can now target it deliberately for 2 hand cards. If V8 always picks magenta, that is the finding, and the fault is the reward rather than the card (ruling H). Read the noise floor before believing any of it - none of the five new lines has one yet. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
